title.en: Volume 432 Biographies 219: Xiao Qijiang, Zhang Yunlan, Tang Xunfang, Jiang Ningxue, Chen Shi, Li Yuandu
title.raw: 卷432 列傳二百十九 萧启江 张运兰 唐训方 蒋凝学 陈湜 李元度

sentences.zh: 列傳二百十九

translations.literal: Biographies, Chapter 219
translations.idiomatic: Biographies, Chapter 219

sentences.zh: 蕭啟江張運蘭唐訓方蔣凝學陳湜李元度

translations.literal: Xiao Qijiang, Zhang Yunlan, Tang Xunfang, Jiang Ningxue, Chen Shi, and Li Yuandu
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Qijiang, Zhang Yunlan, Tang Xunfang, Jiang Ningxue, Chen Shi, and Li Yuandu

sentences.zh: 蕭啟江，字濬川，湖南湘鄉人。

translations.literal: Xiao Qijiang, courtesy name Junchuan, was a native of Xiangxiang in Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Qijiang, styled Junchuan, came from Xiangxiang in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 少賈於蜀，後始折節讀書。

translations.literal: In youth he traded in Shu; only later did he apply himself to study.
translations.idiomatic: As a young man he went into trade in Sichuan, and only afterward turned to serious study.

sentences.zh: 咸豐三年，入塔齊布軍。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xianfeng he entered Taqibu's army.
translations.idiomatic: In 1853 he joined the forces under Taqibu.

sentences.zh: 四年，從平岳州，克武昌、漢陽、興國、大冶、蘄州，敘縣丞，晉秩州同。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he followed in the pacification of Yuezhou, captured Wuchang, Hanyang, Xingguo, Daye, and Qizhou, was recorded for appointment as county assistant magistrate, and was promoted in rank to subprefectural vice commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he took part in pacifying Yuezhou and in capturing Wuchang, Hanyang, Xingguo, Daye, and Qizhou; he was entered for appointment as assistant county magistrate and advanced to the rank of vice subprefect.

sentences.zh: 五年，廣東賊犯湖南，湘撫駱秉章檄啟江募兵協剿，曰果字營，自是獨將一軍。

translations.literal: In the fifth year Guangdong rebels invaded Hunan; the Hunan governor Luo Bingzhang ordered Qijiang to raise troops for joint suppression, called the Guozi Battalion, and from then on he commanded an army alone.
translations.idiomatic: In 1855, when Guangdong rebels entered Hunan, Governor Luo Bingzhang of Hunan directed Qijiang to raise troops for the campaign; his unit was named the Guozi Battalion, and from that point he commanded a separate army of his own.

sentences.zh: 攻茶陵踞匪，率壯士數十人薄南門，賊自民廛躍出，攢矛環刺，啟江手擒數賊，賊莫敢逼。

translations.literal: Attacking the bandits holding Chaling, he led several dozen stalwarts to press close to the south gate; rebels leaped out from among the houses, surrounded him with spears thrust together, yet Qijiang seized several rebels by hand and none dared press him.
translations.idiomatic: When he attacked the rebels entrenched at Chaling, he led a few dozen picked men up to the south gate; the enemy rushed out from the lanes and hemmed him in with spears, but Qijiang seized several of them with his own hands, and none dared close on him.

sentences.zh: 尋會克其城，賊走江西，陷弋陽、興安。

translations.literal: Soon afterward the city was taken in concert; the rebels fled to Jiangxi and captured Yiyang and Xing'an.
translations.idiomatic: The city was soon taken in a joint operation; the rebels fled into Jiangxi and seized Yiyang and Xing'an.

sentences.zh: 啟江偕羅澤南复兩城，進收廣信，賜花翎，擢同知。

translations.literal: Qijiang together with Luo Zinan recovered the two cities, advanced to recover Guangxin, was granted the peacock feather, and was promoted to subprefect.
translations.idiomatic: Qijiang, together with Luo Zinan, recovered both cities and went on to retake Guangxin; he was awarded the peacock feather and promoted to subprefect.

sentences.zh: 六年，劉長佑援江西，總統諸軍，啟江屬焉，駐師瀏陽。

translations.literal: In the sixth year Liu Changyou came to aid Jiangxi as commander-in-chief of the armies; Qijiang was subordinate to him and encamped at Liuyang.
translations.idiomatic: In 1856, Liu Changyou marched to relieve Jiangxi as overall commander; Qijiang served under him and stationed his troops at Liuyang.

sentences.zh: 賊陷萬載，啟江大破之櫧樹潭、大橋、竹阜，遂復萬載；

translations.literal: Rebels captured Wanzai; Qijiang routed them at Zhushutan, Daqiao, and Zhufu, and thus recovered Wanzai.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels took Wanzai, Qijiang routed them at Zhushutan, Daqiao, and Zhufu and recovered the county.

sentences.zh: 而崇通賊复犯瀏陽，援賊大至，撲營，啟江鏖戰敗之，躡至八角亭，毀其壘。

translations.literal: Meanwhile rebels from Chongyang and Tongcheng again invaded Liuyang; relief forces arrived in great numbers and assaulted the camp; Qijiang fought fiercely and defeated them, pursued to Bajiaoting, and destroyed their stockades.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels from Chongyang and Tongcheng then struck Liuyang again; large relief columns came up and stormed his camp, but Qijiang fought them off, pursued them to Bajiaoting, and destroyed their fortifications.

sentences.zh: 會曾國華馳至，偕由洪塘、新昌、上高搗瑞州。

translations.literal: When Zeng Guohua arrived in haste, together they struck at Ruizhou by way of Hongtang, Xinchang, and Shanggao.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng Guohua then hurried up, and together they thrust toward Ruizhou by way of Hongtang, Xinchang, and Shanggao.

sentences.zh: 前軍至登龍橋，擊退袁州賊，進攻新昌、上高，拔之，擢知府。

translations.literal: The vanguard reached Denglong Bridge, repulsed the Yuanzhou rebels, advanced to attack Xinchang and Shanggao, took them, and he was promoted to prefect.
translations.idiomatic: The advance guard reached Denglong Bridge, drove back the Yuanzhou rebels, and pressed on to take Xinchang and Shanggao; Qijiang was promoted to prefect.

sentences.zh: 進攻袁州，啟江與長佑分地扼賊。

translations.literal: Advancing to attack Yuanzhou, Qijiang and Changyou divided the ground to hem in the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: In the attack on Yuanzhou, Qijiang and Changyou divided the approaches to block the enemy.

sentences.zh: 長佑攻西南，啟江攻東北，盡平城外賊屯。

translations.literal: Changyou attacked from the southwest and Qijiang from the northeast, leveling all rebel encampments outside the walls.
translations.idiomatic: Changyou assaulted from the southwest while Qijiang attacked from the northeast, and they cleared every rebel camp outside the city.

sentences.zh: 城賊惶懼，啟江策臨吉賊必來援，設伏敗之，盡奪其輜重。

translations.literal: The rebels in the city were alarmed; Qijiang calculated that Linji rebels would certainly come to relieve them, set an ambush and defeated them, and seized all their baggage and supplies.
translations.idiomatic: The garrison grew fearful; Qijiang judged that Linji rebels would surely come to their aid, laid an ambush, routed them, and captured all their baggage train.

sentences.zh: 尋破賊合山，克分宜，加道銜。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he broke the rebels at Heshan and captured Fenyi, and was given the brevet rank of circuit intendant.
translations.idiomatic: He soon defeated the enemy at Heshan and took Fenyi, and was granted the brevet title of circuit intendant.

sentences.zh: 進攻臨江，七年正月，大捷陰岡嶺，斬其酋。

translations.literal: Advancing to attack Linjiang, in the first month of the seventh year he won a great victory at Yingang Ridge and beheaded their chieftain.
translations.idiomatic: In the assault on Linjiang, in the first month of 1857 he won a great victory at Yingang Ridge and slew the rebel leader.

sentences.zh: 賊勢以孤，乃潛約撫、建、新淦援賊趨太平墟，犯長佑營。

translations.literal: As rebel strength grew isolated, they secretly summoned relief from Fuzhou, Jian, and Xin'gan to advance on Taipingxu and attack Changyou's camp.
translations.idiomatic: With their position growing desperate, the rebels secretly called in reinforcements from Fuzhou, Jian, and Xin'gan, marched on Taipingxu, and struck Changyou's camp.

sentences.zh: 長佑戰失利，營陷，賊乘勢回犯陰岡嶺。

translations.literal: Changyou was defeated in battle and his camp fell; the rebels took advantage of the momentum to turn back and attack Yingang Ridge.
translations.idiomatic: Changyou was beaten and his camp overrun; the enemy then wheeled about and assailed Yingang Ridge.

sentences.zh: 部將田興恕、楊恆升突陣，斬悍酋數人，師從之，賊崩潰，夷其壘四十七。

translations.literal: His subordinates Tian Xingshu and Yang Hengsheng burst through the line and slew several fierce chieftains; the army followed, the rebels collapsed in rout, and forty-seven stockades were leveled.
translations.idiomatic: Subordinates Tian Xingshu and Yang Hengsheng charged the enemy line and killed several of their boldest leaders; the main force followed, the rebels broke and fled, and forty-seven stockades were destroyed.

sentences.zh: 城賊窮蹙乞降，而賊首仍負嵎死拒，乃誘其出戰，啟江揮軍疾進，薄城而登，遂克之，擢道員，加按察使銜。

translations.literal: The rebels in the city, pressed hard, begged to surrender, but their leader still held the corner and resisted to the death; they therefore lured him out to battle, Qijiang led the army forward at speed, pressed close to the wall and mounted it, and thus took the city; he was promoted to circuit commissioner and given the brevet rank of provincial surveillance commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: The besieged rebels, at their wits' end, offered to surrender, yet their chief still clung to the walls and fought on; Qijiang drew him out, then drove his men forward in a rush, scaled the wall, and took the city. He was promoted to circuit commissioner and granted the brevet rank of provincial surveillance commissioner.

sentences.zh: 長佑尋以病歸，劉坤一代之。

translations.literal: Changyou soon returned home on account of illness, and Liu Kunyi replaced him.
translations.idiomatic: Changyou soon went home ill, and Liu Kunyi succeeded to his command.

sentences.zh: 啟江與進攻撫州，連下宜黃、崇仁。

translations.literal: Qijiang advanced with him to attack Fuzhou and in succession took Yihuang and Chongren.
translations.idiomatic: Qijiang joined him in the advance on Fuzhou and in quick succession took Yihuang and Chongren.

sentences.zh: 撫州賊屯樟樹鎮，將伺官軍渡贛襲臨江，啟江與坤一回擊，大破之。

translations.literal: Fuzhou rebels encamped at Zhangshu Town, intending to wait until the government army crossed the Gan to strike at Linjiang; Qijiang and Kunyi turned back and routed them decisively.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels from Fuzhou held Zhangshu Town, planning to strike Linjiang once the government forces crossed the Gan; Qijiang and Kunyi wheeled about and inflicted a crushing defeat.

sentences.zh: 進次上頓，距撫州十五里，築壘甫畢，賊至，迎擊敗之。

translations.literal: He advanced and halted at Shangdun, fifteen li from Fuzhou; his stockades had only just been completed when rebels arrived, and he met them in battle and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: He moved up to Shangdun, fifteen li from Fuzhou; his fortifications were barely finished when the enemy appeared, and he met them head-on and drove them off.

sentences.zh: 進攻高橋，賊棄城遁，追斬千七百有奇。

translations.literal: Advancing to attack Gaoqiao, the rebels abandoned the city and fled; in pursuit more than seventeen hundred were beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: In the assault on Gaoqiao the rebels abandoned the city and fled; the pursuit yielded more than seventeen hundred heads.

sentences.zh: 撫州复，加布政使銜。

translations.literal: Fuzhou was recovered, and he was given the brevet rank of provincial administration commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Fuzhou was recovered, and he received the brevet rank of provincial administration commissioner.

sentences.zh: 九年，賊陷南安，糾眾數万犯贛州，踞新城墟及池江諸地。

translations.literal: In the ninth year rebels captured Nan'an, mustered tens of thousands to invade Ganzhou, and held Xinchengxu and the districts around Chijiang.
translations.idiomatic: In 1859 the rebels took Nan'an, gathered tens of thousands to threaten Ganzhou, and occupied Xinchengxu and the ground along the Chijiang.

sentences.zh: 時曾國籓督援浙軍，啟江率所部從，檄援贛州。

translations.literal: At that time Zeng Guofan was supervising the army sent to aid Zhejiang; Qijiang led his own troops in his train and was ordered to relieve Ganzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng Guofan was then directing the force sent to relieve Zhejiang; Qijiang marched with his division under him and was directed to rescue Ganzhou.

sentences.zh: 啟江遣田勇三千誘賊，賊爭出赴利，啟江摧鋒直進，斬級數千。

translations.literal: Qijiang sent three thousand tianyong as bait; the rebels all rushed out for booty, and Qijiang drove the vanguard straight forward and took several thousand heads.
translations.idiomatic: Qijiang sent three thousand local militiamen forward as bait; the rebels poured out after plunder, and he smashed through with the vanguard, taking several thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 田勇者，江西募農夫防賊，貪鹵獲，倚湘軍無所畏，集者四萬。

translations.literal: Tianyong were Jiangxi farmers recruited to guard against rebels; greedy for spoils and relying on the Hunan army without fear, forty thousand gathered.
translations.idiomatic: The tianyong were Jiangxi farmers raised for local defense; greedy for loot and emboldened by the Hunan troops, they swelled to forty thousand men.

sentences.zh: 啟江曰：「眾而不整必敗。

translations.literal: Qijiang said, "A multitude without discipline is sure to be defeated."
translations.idiomatic: Qijiang warned, "Numbers without order are bound to lose."

sentences.zh: 」禁之不可，遇伏果潰。

translations.literal: He could not forbid them; they met an ambush and indeed collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: He could not restrain them; they walked into an ambush and broke in rout.

sentences.zh: 湘軍為少卻，部將胡中和力戰斷後，復進敗之，平新城墟、池江、小溪、鳳凰城諸賊壘，賊退入南安。

translations.literal: The Hunan army was somewhat forced back; his subordinate Hu Zhonghe fought fiercely to cover the rear, then advanced again and defeated them, leveling the rebel stockades at Xinchengxu, Chijiang, Xiaoxi, and Fenghuangcheng; the rebels withdrew into Nan'an.
translations.idiomatic: The Hunan troops gave ground briefly; subordinate Hu Zhonghe fought a stubborn rearguard action, then pressed forward again and routed the enemy, clearing the rebel camps at Xinchengxu, Chijiang, Xiaoxi, and Fenghuangcheng; the rebels fell back into Nan'an.

sentences.zh: 南安故有二城夾水，賊分屯相犄角，軍至皆棄而走。

translations.literal: Nan'an originally had two cities facing each other across the water; rebels were divided in garrison to support each other in horns, but when the army arrived they all abandoned their posts and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Nan'an had long had twin cities on opposite banks; the rebels held them in mutual support, but at the army's approach they abandoned both and fled.

sentences.zh: 啟江進屯城外青隴、黃隴，結壘自固，令曰：「入城者斬。

translations.literal: Qijiang advanced to encamp outside the city at Qinglong and Huanglong, built stockades to secure himself, and issued the order: "Whoever enters the city shall be beheaded."
translations.idiomatic: Qijiang encamped outside at Qinglong and Huanglong, fortified his position, and ordered, "Anyone who enters the city will be executed."

sentences.zh: 」有頃，賊果還南城，攻之，敗走。

translations.literal: Before long the rebels indeed returned to the south city, attacked it, were defeated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the rebels did return to the southern city; he attacked them and drove them off in defeat.

sentences.zh: 啟江曰：「賊狡而弱，吾直驅之耳！

translations.literal: Qijiang said, "The rebels are cunning but weak; we need only drive straight at them!"
translations.idiomatic: Qijiang said, "They are sly but feeble—we need only press them hard!"

sentences.zh: 」攀堞以登，賊奪西門走，追殺數十里，賜號額埒斯圖巴圖魯。

translations.literal: He scaled the parapet and mounted the wall; the rebels seized the west gate and fled; pursuit and slaughter continued for several tens of li; he was granted the title Elesituo Batulu.
translations.idiomatic: He went up the battlements and over the wall; the rebels bolted through the west gate; the pursuit ran for miles; he was awarded the Manchu title Elesituo Batulu.

sentences.zh: 進信豐，會總兵遮克敦布攻吳家嶺，啟江率中營進。

translations.literal: He advanced to Xinfeng; joining the brigade commander Zhe-kedun-bu in the attack on Wujialing, Qijiang led the central battalion forward.
translations.idiomatic: He marched on Xinfeng, joined Brigadier Zhe-kedun-bu in the assault on Wujialing, and led the central battalion forward.

sentences.zh: 賊萬餘來撲，擊敗之，破先溪橋賊壘，城兵出而夾擊，立解其圍。

translations.literal: More than ten thousand rebels came to assault; he defeated them, broke the rebel stockade at Xianxi Bridge, the city garrison sallied forth and attacked from both sides, and the siege was immediately raised.
translations.idiomatic: Over ten thousand rebels rushed them; he beat them off, stormed the camp at Xianxi Bridge, and with the garrison sallying out in a pincer the siege was lifted at once.

sentences.zh: 時江西郡縣皆复。

translations.literal: At that time all prefectures and counties of Jiangxi had been recovered.
translations.idiomatic: By then every prefecture and county in Jiangxi had been restored.

sentences.zh: 石達開由崇義竄湖南，郴、桂所屬皆告警，啟江馳防。

translations.literal: Shi Dakai fled from Chongyi into Hunan; all districts under Chen and Gui raised alarms, and Qijiang hurried to defend.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Dakai broke out of Chongyi into Hunan; the Chenzhou and Guilin districts were all thrown into alarm, and Qijiang rushed to the defense.

sentences.zh: 賊已由永州竄圍寶慶，啟江自臨、藍趨永州，扼東安，屯白牙市。

translations.literal: The rebels had already fled from Yongzhou to besiege Baoqing; Qijiang marched from Linwu and Lanshan toward Yongzhou, blocked Dong'an, and encamped at Baiyashi.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels had already slipped from Yongzhou to invest Baoqing; Qijiang marched from Linwu and Lanshan toward Yongzhou, seized Dong'an, and encamped at Baiyashi.

sentences.zh: 劉長佑、李續宜解寶慶圍，追至白牙，啟江會軍夾擊，擒其酋楊家廷、馬繼昌於陣。

translations.literal: Liu Changyou and Li Xuyi raised the siege of Baoqing and pursued to Baiya; Qijiang joined the armies in a pincer attack and captured the chieftains Yang Jiating and Ma Jichang in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Changyou and Li Xuyi lifted the siege of Baoqing and pursued the enemy to Baiya; Qijiang joined in a converging attack and took the rebel leaders Yang Jiating and Ma Jichang on the field.

sentences.zh: 賊竄入廣西，陷興安，盡集悍黨大溶江遏追師，遣別賊直犯桂林。

translations.literal: The rebels fled into Guangxi, captured Xing'an, gathered all their fierce bands at Darong River to block the pursuing army, and sent a separate force straight to assault Guilin.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels fled into Guangxi, took Xing'an, massed their hard fighters at the Darong River to hold back pursuit, and detached a column to strike Guilin directly.

sentences.zh: 啟江由全州趨興安，復其城；

translations.literal: Qijiang marched from Quanzhou toward Xing'an and recovered the city.
translations.idiomatic: Qijiang advanced from Quanzhou on Xing'an and recovered the city.

sentences.zh: 攻大溶江，大捷，解桂林圍，以按察使記名。

translations.literal: He attacked at Darong River and won a great victory, raising the siege of Guilin; he was entered on the list for appointment as provincial surveillance commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: At Darong River he won a great victory and relieved Guilin; he was placed on the list for appointment as provincial surveillance commissioner.

sentences.zh: 移軍回湖南。

translations.literal: He shifted his army back to Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: He then moved his army back into Hunan.

sentences.zh: 四川軍事急，命啟江率師往援。

translations.literal: The military situation in Sichuan was urgent, and Qijiang was ordered to lead his army to its aid.
translations.idiomatic: With the fighting in Sichuan growing critical, he was ordered to march his troops to the relief.

sentences.zh: 十年春，甫至，以疾卒於軍。

translations.literal: In the spring of the tenth year, having only just arrived, he died of illness in camp.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of 1860 he had barely arrived when he died of illness in the field.

sentences.zh: 詔贈巡撫，從優賜卹，諡壯果，湖南、江西並建專祠。

translations.literal: An edict posthumously granted him the rank of governor, gave generous mourning favors, and conferred the posthumous title Zhuangguo; special temples were built to him in both Hunan and Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made governor, granted exceptional mourning honors, and given the posthumous name Zhuangguo; dedicated shrines were erected to him in Hunan and Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 其所部留四川，駱秉章用以平賊焉。

translations.literal: His troops remained in Sichuan, and Luo Bingzhang used them to pacify the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: His division stayed in Sichuan, where Luo Bingzhang employed it to finish pacifying the rebels.

sentences.zh: 張運蘭，字凱章，湖南湘鄉人。

translations.literal: Zhang Yunlan, courtesy name Kaizhang, was a native of Xiangxiang in Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yunlan, styled Kaizhang, came from Xiangxiang in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 咸豐初，從王珍轉戰衡、永、郴、桂，積功擢同知。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xianfeng he followed Wang Zhen in campaigns through Hengyang, Yongzhou, Chenzhou, and Guilin, and through accumulated merit was promoted to subprefect.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Xianfeng reign he campaigned under Wang Zhen across Hengyang, Yongzhou, Chenzhou, and Guilin, and rose by merit to subprefect.

sentences.zh: 六年，戰通城，運蘭設三伏，營前斬賊酋張庸忠，擒魯三元，克通城，又大破賊於崇陽白蜺橋，賜花翎。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he fought at Tongcheng; Yunlan set three ambushes, beheaded the rebel chieftain Zhang Yongzhong before the camp, captured Lu Sanyuan, took Tongcheng, and again routed the rebels at Baiwan Bridge in Chongyang; he was granted the peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: In 1856, at Tongcheng, Yunlan laid three ambushes, slew the rebel chief Zhang Yongzhong before his own lines, captured Lu Sanyuan, and took the city; he then routed the enemy again at Baiwan Bridge in Chongyang and was awarded the peacock feather.

sentences.zh: 七年，從王珍援江西，迭捷於臨江、吉安、樂安、新城、廣昌，功皆最。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he followed Wang Zhen to aid Jiangxi and won repeated victories at Linjiang, Ji'an, Le'an, Xincheng, and Guangchang; his merit was foremost in all.
translations.idiomatic: In 1857 he followed Wang Zhen to Jiangxi and won victory after victory at Linjiang, Ji'an, Le'an, Xincheng, and Guangchang, ranking first in merit each time.

sentences.zh: 王珍卒於軍，運蘭與王開化分領其眾。

translations.literal: Wang Zhen died in the army; Yunlan and Wang Kaihua divided command of his forces.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Zhen died in the field, Yunlan and Wang Kaihua divided his troops between them.

sentences.zh: 吉安賊窺永豐，運蘭屢敗之，擢知府。

translations.literal: Ji'an rebels watched for an opening at Yongfeng; Yunlan repeatedly defeated them and was promoted to prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels from Ji'an probed Yongfeng; Yunlan beat them back again and again and was promoted to prefect.

sentences.zh: 又破賊於峽江橋阜灘、獅子山。

translations.literal: He again defeated rebels at Qiaofutan in Xiajiang and at Shizishan.
translations.idiomatic: He defeated them again at Qiaofutan in Xiajiang and at Lion Hill.

sentences.zh: 移軍吉水，扼賊三曲灘，相持數日，血戰十數次，斬賊渠黃錫昆。

translations.literal: He shifted his army to Jishui and blocked the rebels at Sanqu Beach; they faced each other for several days, fought bloody battles more than ten times, and beheaded the rebel leader Huang Xikun.
translations.idiomatic: He moved to Jishui and blocked the enemy at Sanqu Beach; after several days of stalemate and more than a dozen bloody clashes, he slew the rebel commander Huang Xikun.

sentences.zh: 渡贛江，破石達開於硃山橋，達開焚屯而遁，遂解永豐圍，擢道員。

translations.literal: Crossing the Gan River, he defeated Shi Dakai at Zhushan Bridge; Dakai burned his encampment and fled, and thus the siege of Yongfeng was raised; Yunlan was promoted to circuit commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Crossing the Gan, he routed Shi Dakai at Zhushan Bridge; Dakai burned his camp and fled, lifting the siege of Yongfeng, and Yunlan was promoted to circuit commissioner.

sentences.zh: 八年，略定樂安、宜黃，逼建昌，敗賊於厚坪。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he largely pacified Le'an and Yihuang, pressed Jianchang, and defeated rebels at Houping.
translations.idiomatic: In 1858 he brought Le'an and Yihuang largely under control, pressed Jianchang, and defeated the rebels at Houping.

sentences.zh: 破水南賊巢，分剿南源、里塔墟、劉家坑，直搗謝坑，毀賊壘，斬其酋廖雄篙等，复南豐。

translations.literal: He broke the rebel nest south of the river, divided forces to suppress Nanyuan, Litaxu, and Liujiakeng, struck straight at Xiekeng, destroyed rebel stockades, beheaded their chieftains Liao Xionggao and others, and recovered Nanfeng.
translations.idiomatic: He stormed the rebel stronghold south of the river, sent columns against Nanyuan, Litaxu, and Liujiakeng, drove straight into Xiekeng, destroyed the enemy camps, killed leaders including Liao Xionggao, and recovered Nanfeng.

sentences.zh: 建昌之圍始合，五月，克之，加按察使銜。

translations.literal: The siege of Jianchang was at last closed; in the fifth month the city was taken, and he was given the brevet rank of provincial surveillance commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: The ring around Jianchang was finally closed; in the fifth month the city fell, and he received the brevet rank of provincial surveillance commissioner.

sentences.zh: 賊复犯南豐，擊走之，追及新城杭山，降賊眾數千。

translations.literal: Rebels again invaded Nanfeng; he drove them off, pursued to Hangshan in Xincheng, and several thousand rebels surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels struck Nanfeng again; he beat them back, pursued them to Hangshan in Xincheng, and accepted the surrender of several thousand men.

sentences.zh: 時詔起曾國籓督師規浙江，國籓行次江西，賊已入閩，疏調運蘭及蕭啟江率所部從。

translations.literal: At that time an edict recalled Zeng Guofan to command the army planning for Zhejiang; as Guofan passed through Jiangxi the rebels had already entered Fujian, and he memorialized to transfer Yunlan and Xiao Qijiang with their respective troops to follow him.
translations.idiomatic: An edict then recalled Zeng Guofan to take command of the campaign toward Zhejiang; passing through Jiangxi, he found the rebels already in Fujian and requested that Yunlan and Xiao Qijiang march with their divisions under him.

sentences.zh: 會賊陷安仁，別將失利，運蘭進擊，大破之，殲賊數千，克安仁，賜號克圖格爾依巴圖魯。

translations.literal: When rebels captured Anren and another commander was defeated, Yunlan advanced to attack, routed them decisively, destroyed several thousand rebels, recovered Anren, and was granted the title Ketu-ge-er-yi Batulu.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels took Anren and another column was beaten, Yunlan pressed the attack, crushed them, killed several thousand, recovered Anren, and was awarded the Manchu title Ketu-ge-er-yi Batulu.

sentences.zh: 由杉關進剿破賊順昌，回援景德鎮，戰於李村，斬馘二千餘，解散千計。

translations.literal: Advancing through Shan Pass to suppress rebels, he broke them at Shunchang, returned to relieve Jingdezhen, fought at Licun, took more than two thousand heads, and dispersed several thousand more.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced through Shan Pass, defeated the rebels at Shunchang, turned back to relieve Jingdezhen, fought at Licun, took more than two thousand heads, and dispersed another thousand-odd men.

sentences.zh: 九年，援饒州，敗賊於栗樹山，克浮梁，加布政使銜。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he relieved Raozhou, defeated rebels at Lishushan, captured Fuliang, and was given the brevet rank of provincial administration commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In 1859 he relieved Raozhou, defeated the enemy at Chestnut Tree Hill, took Fuliang, and received the brevet rank of provincial administration commissioner.

sentences.zh: 是年秋，粵匪犯湖南寶慶，運蘭回援，疊破賊於宜章、星子、市禾洞，追至廣東連州，破九陂、石塘、白虎墟賊巢，殄賊逾萬，授開歸陳許道。

translations.literal: That autumn Guangdong rebels invaded Baoqing in Hunan; Yunlan returned to aid, repeatedly defeated rebels at Yizhang, Xingzi, and Shihedong, pursued to Lianzhou in Guangdong, broke rebel nests at Jiupi, Shitang, and Baihuxu, destroyed more than ten thousand rebels, and was appointed intendant of the Kaifeng-Chenxu circuit.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn, when Guangdong rebels threatened Baoqing in Hunan, Yunlan marched back to the rescue, won repeated victories at Yizhang, Xingzi, and Shihedong, pursued into Lianzhou in Guangdong, stormed the camps at Jiupi, Shitang, and Baihuxu, killed more than ten thousand of the enemy, and was appointed intendant of the Kaifeng-Chenxu circuit.

sentences.zh: 十年，曾國籓軍祁門，運蘭偕鮑超破賊黟、歙。

translations.literal: In the tenth year Zeng Guofan's army was at Qimen; Yunlan together with Bao Chao defeated rebels in Yi and She.
translations.idiomatic: In 1860, with Zeng Guofan's headquarters at Qimen, Yunlan joined Bao Chao in driving the rebels out of Yi and She.

sentences.zh: 十一年，克休寧，擢福建按察使。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he captured Xiuning and was promoted to Fujian provincial surveillance commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In 1861 he took Xiuning and was promoted to provincial surveillance commissioner of Fujian.

sentences.zh: 再复黟縣，盡夷賊壘。

translations.literal: He recovered Yi County again and leveled all rebel stockades.
translations.idiomatic: He recovered Yi County a second time and destroyed every rebel fort.

sentences.zh: 時運蘭統五千人防徽州，尋移防寧國，值大疫，悍賊麕集，與霆軍力拒之。

translations.literal: At that time Yunlan commanded five thousand men to defend Huizhou; soon he shifted to defend Ningguo; a great epidemic struck, fierce rebels gathered thickly, and together with the Ting Corps he resisted them with all his strength.
translations.idiomatic: He then commanded five thousand men in the defense of Huizhou, soon shifted to Ningguo, and there, amid a raging epidemic and masses of hardened rebels, fought shoulder to shoulder with Bao Chao's Ting Corps to hold them off.

sentences.zh: 同治元年，拔旌德。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tongzhi he captured Jingde.
translations.idiomatic: In 1862 he took Jingde.

sentences.zh: 二年，命援廣東，搗陽山石塋賊巢，降其眾三千，擒巨酋李復猷於連州。

translations.literal: In the second year he was ordered to aid Guangdong, stormed the rebel nest at Shidang in Yangshan, accepted the surrender of three thousand of their number, and at Lianzhou captured the great chieftain Li Fuyou.
translations.idiomatic: In 1863 he was sent to aid Guangdong, smashed the rebel nest at Shidang in Yangshan, accepted three thousand surrenders, and at Lianzhou captured the rebel chieftain Li Fuyou.

sentences.zh: 三年，赴福建按察使任。

translations.literal: In the third year he went to take up his post as Fujian provincial surveillance commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In 1864 he went to Fujian to take up the post of provincial surveillance commissioner.

sentences.zh: 時江、浙逸賊眾猶十餘萬，由江西入閩，蹂汀、漳二郡。

translations.literal: At that time remnant rebels of Jiangsu and Zhejiang still numbered more than a hundred thousand; entering Fujian from Jiangxi, they ravaged the Tingzhou and Zhangzhou prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Remnant rebel bands from Jiangsu and Zhejiang still numbered over a hundred thousand; pouring into Fujian from Jiangxi, they ravaged Tingzhou and Zhangzhou.

sentences.zh: 運蘭率五百人趨武平，遇賊，眾寡不敵，總兵賀世楨、王明高，副將雷照雄皆戰歿；

translations.literal: Yunlan led five hundred men in haste to Wuping, met rebels, and being greatly outnumbered could not prevail; brigade commanders He Shizhen and Wang Minggao and vice commander Lei Zhaoxiong all died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Yunlan hurried to Wuping with five hundred men, ran into the rebels, and was hopelessly outnumbered; Brigadiers He Shizhen and Wang Minggao and Vice Commander Lei Zhaoxiong were all killed in action.

sentences.zh: 運蘭被執，罵賊，支解之。

translations.literal: Yunlan was captured, cursed the rebels, and was dismembered alive.
translations.idiomatic: Yunlan was taken alive; he cursed his captors and was hacked to pieces.

sentences.zh: 事聞，贈巡撫，予騎都尉世職，諡忠毅。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, he was posthumously made governor, granted the hereditary rank of Commandant of Cavalry, and given the posthumous title Zhongyi.
translations.idiomatic: On report of his death he was posthumously made governor, granted a hereditary Commandant of Cavalry, and given the posthumous name Zhongyi.

sentences.zh: 武平及湖南、廣東建專祠。

translations.literal: Special temples were built to him at Wuping and in Hunan and Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: Dedicated shrines were erected to him at Wuping and in Hunan and Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 唐訓方，字義渠，湖南常寧人。

translations.literal: Tang Xunfang, courtesy name Yiqu, was a native of Changning in Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Xunfang, styled Yiqu, came from Changning in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 道光二十年舉人，大挑教諭。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year of Daoguang he passed the provincial examination; in the great selection he was appointed instructor.
translations.idiomatic: He became a provincial graduate in 1840 and, in the imperial selection, was appointed a district instructor.

sentences.zh: 咸豐三年，曾國籓創水師，訓方領副右營，嗣改入陸軍。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xianfeng, when Zeng Guofan created the naval force, Xunfang commanded the deputy right battalion and afterward was transferred to the land army.
translations.idiomatic: In 1853, when Zeng Guofan formed the river flotilla, Xunfang led the deputy right battalion and was later moved into the land forces.

sentences.zh: 從羅澤南克蒲圻，复武昌，又從攻興國金牛堡。

translations.literal: He followed Luo Zinan in capturing Puqi, recovered Wuchang, and again followed in the attack on Jinniubao in Xingguo.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Luo Zinan in taking Puqi and recovering Wuchang, then joined the assault on Jinniubao in Xingguo.

sentences.zh: 國籓命募常寧勇五百人統之，曰訓字營。

translations.literal: Guofan ordered him to raise five hundred Changning braves to command, called the Xunzi Battalion.
translations.idiomatic: Guofan had him raise five hundred men from Changning under his command; the unit was named the Xunzi Battalion.

sentences.zh: 從克田家鎮、蘄州、廣濟，拔黃梅，進軍濯港，敗悍酋羅大綱。

translations.literal: He followed in the capture of Tianjiazhen, Qizhou, and Guangji, took Huangmei, advanced to Zhuogang, and defeated the fierce chieftain Luo Dagang.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in capturing Tianjiazhen, Qizhou, and Guangji, seized Huangmei, advanced to Zhuogang, and defeated the rebel commander Luo Dagang.

sentences.zh: 是夕，賊謀襲大營，訓方巡營驚覺，賊退走。

translations.literal: That night the rebels plotted a night assault on the main camp; Xunfang on patrol was startled awake, and the rebels withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: That night the rebels planned a raid on the main camp; Xunfang, making his rounds, detected them in time and they fled.

sentences.zh: 明日，攻孔壟街口，訓方率壯士踏肩陟高墉，諸軍乘之，遂破孔壟。

translations.literal: The next day, attacking Konglong Street mouth, Xunfang led stalwarts who stepped on one another's shoulders to climb the high wall; the armies followed and thus broke Konglong.
translations.idiomatic: The next day, assaulting the entrance to Konglong Street, Xunfang led picked men up the high wall on one another's shoulders; the main force followed and took Konglong.

sentences.zh: 五年，從澤南援江西，克弋陽、興安、廣信、德興、浮梁。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he followed Zinan to aid Jiangxi and captured Yiyang, Xing'an, Guangxin, Dexing, and Fuliang.
translations.idiomatic: In 1855 he followed Zinan to Jiangxi and took Yiyang, Xing'an, Guangxin, Dexing, and Fuliang.

sentences.zh: 援義寧賊屯城外雞鳴、鳳凰二山，與城犄角。

translations.literal: Relieving Yining, rebels were encamped outside the city on Jiming and Fenghuang mountains, supporting the city in horns.
translations.idiomatic: In the relief of Yining, rebels held Jiming and Fenghuang hills outside the walls in mutual support with the garrison.

sentences.zh: 訓方逼雞鳴山下，督隊先登，賊驚潰，乘勝拔其城。

translations.literal: Xunfang pressed close beneath Jiming Mountain, urged his company to mount first, the rebels fled in alarm, and taking advantage of victory he stormed the city.
translations.idiomatic: Xunfang pressed the foot of Jiming Hill, drove his men to scale first, routed the startled garrison, and pressed on to take the city.

sentences.zh: 從澤南援武漢，克蒲圻，進攻武昌。

translations.literal: He followed Zinan to aid Wuhan, captured Puqi, and advanced to attack Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Zinan to the relief of Wuhan, took Puqi again, and pressed the attack on Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 累擢知府，賜花翎。

translations.literal: Through repeated promotions he rose to prefect and was granted the peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: He rose step by step to prefect and was awarded the peacock feather.

sentences.zh: 六年正月，率三百人夜由鮎魚套至藕塘，奪二壘，又破援賊於豹子海。

translations.literal: In the first month of the sixth year he led three hundred men by night from Nianyu Bay to Outang, seized two stockades, and again defeated relief rebels at Baozihai.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of 1856 he led three hundred men by night from Nianyu Bay to Lotus Pond, took two stockades, and routed relief forces at Baozihai.

sentences.zh: 會襄陽土匪高二倡亂，圍府城，巡撫胡林翼令訓方偕舒保馬隊往剿。

translations.literal: When bandits led by Gao Er in Xiangyang rose in revolt and besieged the prefectural city, Governor Hu Linyi ordered Xunfang to go with Shu Bao's cavalry to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: When the Xiangyang bandit Gao Er rebelled and besieged the prefectural seat, Governor Hu Linyi sent Xunfang with Shu Bao's cavalry to put them down.

sentences.zh: 破賊於峪山，援賊至，又敗之。

translations.literal: He defeated rebels at Yushan; relief forces arrived and he defeated them again.
translations.idiomatic: He routed them at Yushan; when reinforcements came up, he beat them again.

sentences.zh: 進克樊城，追至呂堰驛，斬女賊宋氏。

translations.literal: He advanced and captured Fancheng, pursued to Luyan Post, and beheaded the female rebel Song.
translations.idiomatic: He took Fancheng, pursued the enemy to Luyan Post, and slew the rebel woman Song.

sentences.zh: 援宜昌，破賊於南漳，權襄陽知府。

translations.literal: He relieved Yichang, defeated rebels at Nanzhang, and acted as prefect of Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: He marched to relieve Yichang, defeated the enemy at Nanzhang, and served as acting prefect of Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 七年二月，川匪劉尚義犯宜城，揚言趨荊門，而使南漳賊襲府城，訓方備之，急扼武安堰，賊奔據武安城，進攻之。

translations.literal: In the second month of the seventh year Sichuan rebels under Liu Shangyi invaded Yicheng, declared they would march on Jingmen, and had Nanzhang rebels strike the prefectural city; Xunfang prepared against them, hastily blocked Wu'an Weir, the rebels fled to hold Wu'an city, and he advanced to attack.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of 1857, Sichuan rebels under Liu Shangyi attacked Yicheng, claiming they would march on Jingmen while Nanzhang rebels struck the prefectural seat; Xunfang made ready, seized Wu'an Weir, and when the enemy fell back into Wu'an city, pressed the attack.

sentences.zh: 會都統巴揚阿來招降，訓方進剿高二於璩灣，乘雪夜進攻，擒之；

translations.literal: When Commander-in-chief Bayang'a came to accept surrenders, Xunfang advanced to suppress Gao Er at Quwan, attacked on a snowy night, and captured him.
translations.idiomatic: Commander Bayang'a then arrived to negotiate surrenders; Xunfang pressed Gao Er at Quwan, attacked on a snowy night, and took him prisoner.

sentences.zh: 而巴揚阿所撫賊复叛，掠鄖、房、保山、竹山、竹谿、保康、興山。

translations.literal: But rebels whom Bayang'a had pacified rebelled again and plundered Yun, Fang, Baoshan, Zhushan, Zhuxi, Baokang, and Xingshan.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels whom Bayang'a had brought over then rose again, ravaging Yun, Fang, Baoshan, Zhushan, Zhuxi, Baokang, and Xingshan.

sentences.zh: 訓方會陝西軍連破之武當山金頂，斬其渠，餘賊降。

translations.literal: Xunfang joined Shaanxi troops in repeatedly defeating them at the Golden Summit of Wudang Mountain, beheaded their leader, and the remaining rebels surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Xunfang, with Shaanxi troops, repeatedly defeated them at the Golden Summit on Wudang Mountain, killed their leader, and the rest surrendered.

sentences.zh: 襄郡悉定。

translations.literal: The entire Xiangyang prefecture was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: The whole Xiangyang region was brought to order.

sentences.zh: 先以克武漢論功以道員記名，至是加按察使銜，授湖北督糧道。

translations.literal: Earlier, for merit in recovering Wuhan he had been entered on the list as circuit commissioner; now he was given the brevet rank of provincial surveillance commissioner and appointed grain intendant of Hubei.
translations.idiomatic: He had already been entered on the list for circuit commissioner for his part in recovering Wuhan; now he received the brevet rank of provincial surveillance commissioner and was made grain intendant of Hubei.

sentences.zh: 陳玉成合捻匪犯蘄、黃，訓方自襄陽赴援，連戰敗賊，進屯張家塝。

translations.literal: Chen Yucheng together with Nian rebels invaded Qizhou and Huangzhou; Xunfang marched from Xiangyang to aid, defeated rebels in successive battles, and advanced to encamp at Zhangjiabang.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yucheng joined Nian rebels in attacking Qizhou and Huangzhou; Xunfang hurried from Xiangyang, won a string of victories, and encamped at Zhangjiabang.

sentences.zh: 胡林翼令於蘄州境內建碉卡，訓方以二千人守之，賊迭來攻，皆擊退，賜號奇齊葉勒特依巴圖魯。

translations.literal: Hu Linyi ordered blockhouses built within Qizhou territory; Xunfang garrisoned them with two thousand men; rebels came to attack repeatedly and were all repulsed; he was granted the title Qiqiyeleteyi Batulu.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Linyi ordered fortified posts built in Qizhou; Xunfang held them with two thousand men and beat back repeated assaults; he was awarded the Manchu title Qiqiyeleteyi Batulu.

sentences.zh: 調援臨淮。

translations.literal: He was transferred to relieve Linhuai.
translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned to relieve Linhuai.

sentences.zh: 尋以李續賓軍覆三河，回防湖北，屯陳德園。

translations.literal: Soon afterward, because Li Xubin's army was destroyed at Sanhe, he returned to defend Hubei and encamped at Chendeyuan.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Xubin's army was wiped out at Sanhe, he returned to defend Hubei and encamped at Chendeyuan.

sentences.zh: 九年，會攻太湖，賊圍鮑超於小池驛，多隆阿不能救，令訓方移軍近鮑營為接應。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, in the joint attack on Taihu, rebels besieged Bao Chao at Xiaochi Post; Duolong'a could not save him and ordered Xunfang to move his army close to Bao's camp as support.
translations.idiomatic: In 1859, during the joint assault on Taihu, rebels besieged Bao Chao at Xiaochi Post; Duolong'a could not relieve him and ordered Xunfang to move up near Bao's camp as support.

sentences.zh: 甫至，築壘未就，為賊所乘，乃退屯新倉。

translations.literal: He had only just arrived when his stockades were not yet finished and rebels took advantage; he therefore withdrew to encamp at Xincang.
translations.idiomatic: He had barely arrived when his fortifications were still unfinished and the enemy struck; he fell back to Xincang.

sentences.zh: 十年，解軍事，赴糧道任。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was relieved of military duties and went to take up the grain intendant post.
translations.idiomatic: In 1860 he left the field and took up his post as grain intendant.

sentences.zh: 未幾，連擢湖北布政使。

translations.literal: Before long he was promoted in succession to Hubei provincial administration commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to provincial administration commissioner of Hubei.

sentences.zh: 十一年，胡林翼駐軍英山，病甚。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year Hu Linyi was stationed at Yingshan and was gravely ill.
translations.idiomatic: In 1861 Hu Linyi lay gravely ill with his headquarters at Yingshan.

sentences.zh: 賊上犯黃州，抵灄口，武昌震動，訛言繁興。

translations.literal: Rebels advanced to invade Huangzhou and reached Zhuankou; Wuchang was shaken and rumors flourished.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels pushed up into Huangzhou and reached Zhuankou; Wuchang was thrown into alarm and rumors spread wildly.

sentences.zh: 訓方處以鎮靜，誅亂民數人，人心始定。

translations.literal: Xunfang handled matters with calm, executed several disorderly civilians, and people's minds were at last settled.
translations.idiomatic: Xunfang kept his composure, executed several agitators, and public order was restored.

sentences.zh: 灄口賊亦擊退。

translations.literal: The rebels at Zhuankou were also driven off.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels at Zhuankou were driven off as well.

sentences.zh: 同治元年，安徽巡撫李續宜因母喪奪情，請假回籍，舉訓方自代，命暫行署理。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tongzhi, Anhui Governor Li Xuyi, having been released from mourning obligations for his mother, asked leave to return home and recommended Xunfang to replace him; he was ordered to act temporarily in the post.
translations.idiomatic: In 1862, when Anhui Governor Li Xuyi was released from mourning and went home on leave, he recommended Xunfang as his replacement, and Xunfang was ordered to serve as acting governor.

sentences.zh: 苗沛霖反側久，遂叛，安徽諸軍皆不能制。

translations.literal: Miao Peilin had long wavered and at last rebelled; none of the Anhui armies could control him.
translations.idiomatic: Miao Peilin, long unreliable, finally rebelled, and none of the Anhui forces could bring him to heel.

sentences.zh: 二年，僧格林沁大軍至，始平之。

translations.literal: In the second year Sengge Rinchen's great army arrived and only then pacified him.
translations.idiomatic: In 1863 Sengge Rinchen's main force arrived and at last suppressed him.

sentences.zh: 撫循降圩，收其兵械，奏移鳳臺，治下蔡雉河集，增立渦陽縣。

translations.literal: He soothed surrendered stockaded villages, collected their arms, memorialized to move Fengtai, administer Xiaheji at Xiacai, and establish the new county of Woyang.
translations.idiomatic: He pacified surrendered stockades, collected their weapons, memorialized to relocate Fengtai, administer Xiaheji at Xiacai, and create the new county of Woyang.

sentences.zh: 都統富明阿奏劾訓方，降調。

translations.literal: Commander Fuming'a memorialized to impeach Xunfang, and he was demoted and transferred.
translations.idiomatic: Commander Fuming'a impeached Xunfang, and he was demoted and transferred.

sentences.zh: 三年，署湖北按察使，尋署巡撫，授直隸布政使，兼統練軍出省防剿。

translations.literal: In the third year he acted as Hubei provincial surveillance commissioner, soon acted as governor, was appointed Zhili provincial administration commissioner, and concurrently commanded the trained army in expedition outside the province for defense and suppression.
translations.idiomatic: In 1864 he served as acting provincial surveillance commissioner of Hubei, soon as acting governor, then was appointed provincial administration commissioner of Zhili and led the trained troops on campaign beyond the province.

sentences.zh: 七年，西捻平。

translations.literal: In the seventh year the western Nian were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: In 1868 the western Nian rebels were suppressed.

sentences.zh: 請開缺省墓。

translations.literal: He requested leave of office to return home for tomb maintenance.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to resign and return home to tend his family's graves.

sentences.zh: 光緒三年，卒於家。

translations.literal: In the third year of Guangxu he died at home.
translations.idiomatic: He died at home in 1877.

sentences.zh: 湖北請祀名宦祠。

translations.literal: Hubei requested that he be enshrined in the temple of eminent officials.
translations.idiomatic: Hubei petitioned for his enshrinement in the hall of distinguished officials.

sentences.zh: 蔣凝學，字之純，湖南湘鄉人。

translations.literal: Jiang Ningxue, courtesy name Zhichun, was a native of Xiangxiang in Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Ningxue, styled Zhichun, came from Xiangxiang in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 咸豐初，在籍治鄉團。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xianfeng he organized local militia in his native place.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Xianfeng reign he organized local defense forces in his home district.

sentences.zh: 五年，從羅澤南克武昌，獎國子監典簿。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he followed Luo Zinan in capturing Wuchang and was rewarded with the post of director of studies in the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: In 1855 he followed Luo Zinan in taking Wuchang and was rewarded with a post in the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 六年，率湘左兩營從巡撫胡林翼攻武昌。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he led the two Xiangzuo battalions with Governor Hu Linyi to attack Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: In 1856 he led two battalions under Governor Hu Linyi in the assault on Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 屯賽湖堤，引江水入湖，合長圍，進薄城下，平賊壘十餘。

translations.literal: He encamped on the Saihu embankment, diverted river water into the lake, joined the long encirclement, advanced close beneath the walls, and leveled more than ten rebel stockades.
translations.idiomatic: He encamped on the Saihu dike, diverted the river into the lake, joined the long siege line, pressed up to the walls, and destroyed more than ten rebel camps.

sentences.zh: 武昌复，論功擢知縣。

translations.literal: When Wuchang was recovered, he was promoted to county magistrate for merit.
translations.idiomatic: When Wuchang fell, he was promoted to county magistrate for his service.

sentences.zh: 從克黃州、大冶、興國，逼九江。

translations.literal: He followed in the capture of Huangzhou, Daye, and Xingguo and pressed Jiujiang.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in capturing Huangzhou, Daye, and Xingguo and pressed the attack on Jiujiang.

sentences.zh: 七年，分統三營屯北岸陸家嘴​​，攻小池口，屢戰皆捷。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he separately commanded three battalions encamped at Lujiazui on the north bank, attacked Xiaochikou, and won repeated victories in battle.
translations.idiomatic: In 1857 he commanded three battalions on the north bank at Lujiazui, attacked Xiaochikou, and won victory after victory.

sentences.zh: 都興阿檄攻童司簰。

translations.literal: Duxing'a ordered an attack on Tongsipai.
translations.idiomatic: Duxing'a ordered an assault on Tongsipai.

sentences.zh: 童司簰背江據湖，通黃梅要隘，賊五六萬踞之。

translations.literal: Tongsipai lay with its back to the river and held the lake, connecting with the strategic pass of Huangmei; fifty or sixty thousand rebels occupied it.
translations.idiomatic: Tongsipai stood with the river at its back and the lake before it, commanding the Huangmei pass; fifty or sixty thousand rebels held it.

sentences.zh: 至則賊數搏戰，凝學堅持不退。

translations.literal: On arrival the rebels fought repeatedly; Ningxue held firm and would not withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: On arrival the enemy fought again and again; Ningxue held his ground and refused to pull back.

sentences.zh: 尋陳玉成來援，眾議退兵，凝學曰：「童司簰不克，水師往來失所據，九江之師亦掣肘，勢所必爭。

translations.literal: Soon Chen Yucheng came to relieve them; the host debated withdrawal; Ningxue said, "If Tongsipai is not taken, the navy will lose its footing in coming and going, and the Jiujiang army will also be hampered—this is ground that must be contested."
translations.idiomatic: When Chen Yucheng came to their aid, many urged retreat; Ningxue said, "Unless we take Tongsipai, the fleet will have no secure base and the Jiujiang campaign will be crippled—we must fight for this place."

sentences.zh: 」請增兵千人，宵濟合水師，連日鏖戰，破之，平賊壘數十，進克黃梅，擢同知。

translations.literal: He requested an additional thousand troops, crossed by night to join the navy, fought fierce battles for successive days, broke them, leveled dozens of rebel stockades, advanced to capture Huangmei, and was promoted to subprefect.
translations.idiomatic: He asked for another thousand men, crossed by night to join the fleet, fought day after day, broke the enemy, destroyed dozens of camps, took Huangmei, and was promoted to subprefect.

sentences.zh: 八年，會攻九江府城。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he joined in the attack on Jiujiang prefectural city.
translations.idiomatic: In 1858 he joined the assault on Jiujiang.

sentences.zh: 凝學穴地道迤東而南，地雷發，壞城垣百餘丈，從缺口入，殲賊甚眾，擢知府，賜花翎。

translations.literal: Ningxue dug a tunnel eastward and then south; a land mine was fired, destroying more than a hundred zhang of wall; he entered through the breach and destroyed very many rebels; he was promoted to prefect and granted the peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: Ningxue drove a mine tunnel east and then south; the blast breached more than a hundred zhang of wall; he poured through the gap and slaughtered a great many defenders; he was promoted to prefect and awarded the peacock feather.

sentences.zh: 連复麻城、黃安，擢道員。

translations.literal: He recovered Macheng and Huang'an in succession and was promoted to circuit commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He recovered Macheng and Huang'an in turn and was promoted to circuit commissioner.

sentences.zh: 十月，李續賓三河軍覆，官文檄凝學間道遏剿。

translations.literal: In the tenth month Li Xubin's army was destroyed at Sanhe; Guanwen ordered Ningxue by a side route to intercept and suppress.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month, when Li Xubin's army was destroyed at Sanhe, Guanwen ordered Ningxue to move by a side route and block the enemy.

sentences.zh: 會多隆阿、鮑超擊賊於宿松花亭子，破之。

translations.literal: Duolong'a and Bao Chao joined in attacking rebels at Songtingzi in Suzhou and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Duolong'a and Bao Chao met the enemy at Songtingzi in Suzhou and routed them.

sentences.zh: 賊退太湖、潛山，凝學駐防荊橋。

translations.literal: The rebels retreated to Taihu and Qianshan; Ningxue garrisoned Jingqiao.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels fell back toward Taihu and Qianshan; Ningxue garrisoned Jingqiao.

sentences.zh: 九年，移屯黃州羅田，會攻太湖。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he shifted camp to Luotian in Huangzhou and joined in the attack on Taihu.
translations.idiomatic: In 1859 he moved to Luotian in Huangzhou and joined the assault on Taihu.

sentences.zh: 十二月，陳​​玉成大舉來援，凝學移軍龍家涼亭，與鮑超小池驛之軍為犄角，留四營遏太湖東門，城賊出，擊退之。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month Chen Yucheng came in force to relieve; Ningxue moved his army to Longjialiangting, supported Bao Chao's force at Xiaochi Post in horns, left four battalions to block Taihu's east gate, and when city rebels sallied forth drove them back.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Chen Yucheng marched up in force; Ningxue shifted to Longjialiangting to support Bao Chao at Xiaochi Post, left four battalions to hold Taihu's east gate, and beat back a sortie from the city.

sentences.zh: 十年正月，鮑營被圍急，凝學進援，甫拔營，賊大隊來抄，凝學揮軍截擊，多隆阿率馬隊應之，戰竟日，擒斬二千餘。

translations.literal: In the first month of the tenth year Bao's camp was urgently besieged; Ningxue advanced to relieve; he had only just broken camp when a large rebel force came to outflank; Ningxue led the army to intercept; Duolong'a brought cavalry to respond; they fought all day and captured or beheaded more than two thousand.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of 1860 Bao's camp was hard pressed; Ningxue marched to relieve him; as he was breaking camp a large enemy column tried to cut him off; Ningxue turned to intercept, Duolong'a brought up cavalry, and after a full day's fighting they killed or captured more than two thousand.

sentences.zh: 乘勝攻羅山，衝賊壘，諸軍合擊，賊大潰，加鹽運使銜。

translations.literal: Taking advantage of victory he attacked Luoshan, charged rebel stockades, the armies joined in assault, and the rebels collapsed in great rout; he was given the brevet rank of salt transport commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Pressing the advantage, he stormed Luoshan, smashed the enemy camps in a combined assault, and routed them completely; he received the brevet rank of salt transport commissioner.

sentences.zh: 十一年，陳玉成復犯湖北，凝學回援武昌縣，敗賊赤壁山下，復其城。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year Chen Yucheng again invaded Hubei; Ningxue returned to aid Wuchang County, defeated rebels below Chibi Mountain, and recovered the city.
translations.idiomatic: In 1861 Chen Yucheng invaded Hubei again; Ningxue hurried back to Wuchang County, routed the enemy below Red Cliff Hill, and recovered the city.

sentences.zh: 會總兵成大吉等攻黃州數月不下，詔降賊目劉維楨，复蘄州，選出眾五百人為忠義營，使維楨詐稱援軍，誘城賊出，擊之，遂克黃州，以道員記名，加布政使銜。

translations.literal: Brigadier Cheng Daji and others had attacked Huangzhou for months without success; an edict accepted the surrender of rebel leader Liu Weizhen; Qizhou was recovered; five hundred picked men were chosen as the Loyalty Battalion; Weizhen was made to feign relief troops, lure city rebels out, and strike them; thus Huangzhou was taken; Ningxue was entered on the list as circuit commissioner and given the brevet rank of provincial administration commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Brigadier Cheng Daji had besieged Huangzhou for months without success; the court accepted the defection of rebel leader Liu Weizhen; Qizhou was recovered; Ningxue formed a Loyalty Battalion of five hundred picked men and had Weizhen pose as reinforcements to draw the garrison out; Huangzhou then fell; he was entered on the list for circuit commissioner and granted the brevet rank of provincial administration commissioner.

sentences.zh: 苗沛霖叛，陷壽州，凝學進屯六安，克霍丘，增募水陸軍。

translations.literal: Miao Peilin rebelled and captured Shouzhou; Ningxue advanced to encamp at Lu'an, captured Huoqiu, and increased recruitment for land and river forces.
translations.idiomatic: When Miao Peilin rebelled and took Shouzhou, Ningxue advanced to Lu'an, took Huoqiu, and raised additional land and river troops.

sentences.zh: 苗黨姚有志、潘塏等乞降，各圩多反正，授甘肅安肅道。

translations.literal: Miao partisans Yao Youzhi, Pan Kai, and others begged to surrender; many stockades returned to allegiance; he was appointed intendant of the Ansu circuit in Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: Miao followers Yao Youzhi, Pan Kai, and others offered to surrender; many stockades came back over; he was appointed intendant of the Ansu circuit in Gansu.

sentences.zh: 同治元年，移屯潁州。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tongzhi he shifted camp to Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In 1862 he moved his headquarters to Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 二年，粵匪李世賢北竄，凝學移軍舒城，擊敗之，又追敗之六安，賊引去。

translations.literal: In the second year Guangdong rebels under Li Shixian fled north; Ningxue moved his army to Shucheng, defeated them, pursued and defeated them again at Lu'an, and the rebels withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: In 1863 the Guangdong rebel Li Shixian broke north; Ningxue moved to Shucheng, beat him off, pursued him to Lu'an and defeated him again, and the enemy withdrew.

sentences.zh: 苗沛霖复圍壽州，凝學回援，破賊於牛尾岡。

translations.literal: Miao Peilin again besieged Shouzhou; Ningxue returned to aid and defeated rebels at Niuyigang.
translations.idiomatic: When Miao Peilin besieged Shouzhou again, Ningxue marched back and routed the enemy at Niuyigang.

sentences.zh: 壽州尋陷，凝學坐救援不力，褫布政使銜，仍駐防潁州。

translations.literal: Shouzhou soon fell; Ningxue was punished for ineffective relief, stripped of his brevet provincial administration commissioner rank, and still garrisoned Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Shouzhou soon fell; Ningxue was blamed for failing to relieve it, stripped of his brevet provincial administration commissioner rank, and remained at Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 會僧格林沁督師剿沛霖，凝學克霍丘各圩，水師分駐三河尖、臨淮關，進破黃梁集，克潁上，收附近城各圩，斬賊黨苗呆和、苗呆花，复懷遠。

translations.literal: When Sengge Rinchen commanded the army to suppress Peilin, Ningxue captured the stockades around Huoqiu; the navy was divided between Sanhejian and Linhuaiguan; he advanced to break Huangliangji, captured Yingshang, recovered nearby walled villages, beheaded the Miao partisans Miao Daihe and Miao Daihua, and recovered Huaiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: When Sengge Rinchen took command against Peilin, Ningxue cleared the stockades around Huoqiu; the fleet held Sanhejian and Linhuaiguan; he stormed Huangliangji, took Yingshang, brought in the surrounding stockades, killed Miao partisans Miao Daihe and Miao Daihua, and recovered Huaiyuan.

sentences.zh: 沛霖勢日蹙，遂走死。

translations.literal: Peilin's position grew daily more desperate, and he fled and died.
translations.idiomatic: Peilin's position collapsed; he fled and died.

sentences.zh: 三年，粵匪陳得才等糾眾三十萬自陝西回竄，圖救江寧。

translations.literal: In the third year Guangdong rebels Chen Decai and others mustered three hundred thousand men fleeing back from Shaanxi, intending to relieve Jiangning.
translations.idiomatic: In 1864 Chen Decai and other Guangdong rebels gathered three hundred thousand men fleeing back from Shaanxi, aiming to relieve Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 凝學屯英山，遏賊金家鋪，敗之。

translations.literal: Ningxue encamped at Yingshan, blocked the rebels at Jinjiapu, and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Ningxue held Yingshan, blocked the enemy at Jinjiapu, and routed them.

sentences.zh: 賊復自麻城犯霍山，凝學退石家嘴，與按察使英翰相犄角，伺賊過狙擊，殪千餘人，拔出難民數千。

translations.literal: Rebels again invaded Huoshan from Macheng; Ningxue withdrew to Shijiazui and with Provincial Surveillance Commissioner Ying Han supported each other in horns, waited for rebels to pass and ambushed them, killed more than a thousand, and rescued several thousand refugees.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy struck Huoshan again from Macheng; Ningxue fell back to Shijiazui and, in concert with Provincial Surveillance Commissioner Ying Han, ambushed them as they passed, killing more than a thousand and rescuing several thousand civilians.

sentences.zh: 英山解嚴，复布政使銜。

translations.literal: The alarm at Yingshan was lifted, and his brevet provincial administration commissioner rank was restored.
translations.idiomatic: The emergency at Yingshan ended, and his brevet provincial administration commissioner rank was restored.

sentences.zh: 進援湖北，收復羅田、蘄水、麻城三縣，解蔡家河圍。

translations.literal: He advanced to aid Hubei, recovered the three counties of Luotian, Qishui, and Macheng, and raised the siege of Caijiahe.
translations.idiomatic: He marched into Hubei, recovered Luotian, Qishui, and Macheng, and lifted the siege of Caijiahe.

sentences.zh: 賊复竄安徽，凝學躡追，沿途襲擊，繞出賊前，遏之霍山長嶺庵。

translations.literal: Rebels again fled into Anhui; Ningxue pursued close, struck along the route, circled ahead of the rebels, and blocked them at Changling'an in Huoshan.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels fled back into Anhui; Ningxue pursued hard, harried them along the way, got ahead of them, and blocked them at Changling'an in Huoshan.

sentences.zh: 路險，賊不虞兵猝至，多墜澗死，降者三四萬，賊首陳得才仰藥死。

translations.literal: The road was perilous; rebels did not expect troops to arrive suddenly; many fell into ravines and died; thirty or forty thousand surrendered; the rebel leader Chen Decai took poison and died.
translations.idiomatic: On the narrow road the enemy was caught unawares; many plunged into ravines and died; thirty or forty thousand surrendered; rebel chief Chen Decai took poison and died.

sentences.zh: 簡降眾為步隊五營、馬隊三營，餘悉遣散。

translations.literal: He selected the surrendered masses into five infantry battalions and three cavalry battalions, and dispersed all the rest.
translations.idiomatic: He organized the surrendered men into five infantry battalions and three cavalry battalions and discharged the rest.

sentences.zh: 是年冬，陝甘總督楊岳斌奏調凝學赴甘肅，行次樊城，會霆軍譁變。

translations.literal: That winter Shaanxi-Gansu Governor Yang Yuebin memorialized to transfer Ningxue to Gansu; on the road at Fancheng he encountered the Ting Corps mutiny.
translations.idiomatic: That winter Governor Yang Yuebin of Shaanxi and Gansu requested Ningxue's transfer to Gansu; at Fancheng he ran into the mutiny of Bao Chao's Ting Corps.

sentences.zh: 凝學所部亦以欠餉不靖，請於巡撫鄭敦謹，借款資遣湘左八營，留忠義營於湖北，自請回籍養病。

translations.literal: Ningxue's own troops were also unsettled for lack of pay; he requested of Governor Zheng Dunjin a loan to pay off and dismiss the eight Xiangzuo battalions, left the Loyalty Battalion in Hubei, and asked to return home to convalesce.
translations.idiomatic: His own troops were restless for lack of pay; he borrowed from Governor Zheng Dunjin to pay off and dismiss the eight Xiangzuo battalions, left the Loyalty Battalion in Hubei, and asked to go home to recover his health.

sentences.zh: 命兩月假滿仍赴甘肅。

translations.literal: He was ordered that when two months' leave ended he should still proceed to Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to proceed to Gansu when his two months' leave ended.

sentences.zh: 五年，募湘勇二千，號安字營。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he recruited two thousand Hunan braves, called the Anzi Battalion.
translations.idiomatic: In 1866 he raised two thousand Hunan troops as the Anzi Battalion.

sentences.zh: 至西安，巡撫劉蓉奏請凝學屯涇州，兼顧關隴。

translations.literal: Reaching Xi'an, Governor Liu Rong memorialized requesting that Ningxue encamp at Jingzhou and also watch over Guanlong.
translations.idiomatic: At Xi'an, Governor Liu Rong asked that Ningxue garrison Jingzhou and cover the Guanlong region.

sentences.zh: 六月，敗回匪於華亭，與提督雷正綰、總兵張在山等約夾擊，深入被圍，士卒死傷七百餘人，總兵周太和、周清貴，副將黃德太等均歿於陣。

translations.literal: In the sixth month he defeated Hui rebels at Huating; agreeing with Provincial Commander Lei Zhengwan, Brigadier Zhang Zaishan, and others on a pincer attack, he advanced deep and was surrounded; more than seven hundred soldiers were killed or wounded; Brigadiers Zhou Taihe and Zhou Qinggui and Vice Commander Huang Detai all died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month he defeated Muslim rebels at Huating; in a planned pincer with Provincial Commander Lei Zhengwan and Brigadier Zhang Zaishan he pushed too far and was surrounded; more than seven hundred of his men were killed or wounded; Brigadiers Zhou Taihe and Zhou Qinggui and Vice Commander Huang Detai were among the dead.

sentences.zh: 凝學潰圍出，屯平涼，轉戰而前，至省城，署蘭州道。

translations.literal: Ningxue broke out of the encirclement, encamped at Pingliang, fought forward in turn, reached the provincial capital, and acted as Lanzhou circuit intendant.
translations.idiomatic: Ningxue broke out, encamped at Pingliang, fought his way forward to the provincial capital, and served as acting intendant of Lanzhou.

sentences.zh: 六年八月，回匪犯蘭州，守城兵僅凝學所部千餘人，登陴固守，屢出奇兵焚賊壘，賊尋退，以按察使記名。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the sixth year Hui rebels attacked Lanzhou; the garrison was only a little more than a thousand of Ningxue's troops; he mounted the walls and held firm, repeatedly sent surprise forces to burn rebel stockades, the rebels soon withdrew, and he was entered on the list for provincial surveillance commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of 1867 Muslim rebels attacked Lanzhou; only a little over a thousand of Ningxue's men held the walls; he mounted a stubborn defense, repeatedly sallied to burn enemy camps, drove them off, and was placed on the list for provincial surveillance commissioner.

sentences.zh: 八年，署按察使。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he acted as provincial surveillance commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In 1869 he served as acting provincial surveillance commissioner.

sentences.zh: 九年，复署蘭州道，擢山西按察使。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he again acted as Lanzhou circuit intendant and was promoted to Shanxi provincial surveillance commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In 1870 he again served as acting intendant of Lanzhou and was promoted to provincial surveillance commissioner of Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 光緒元年，遷陝西布政使。

translations.literal: In the first year of Guangxu he was transferred to Shaanxi provincial administration commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In 1875 he was transferred to provincial administration commissioner of Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 四年，以病解官，未行而卒。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he resigned office on account of illness and died before departing.
translations.idiomatic: In 1878 he resigned on grounds of illness and died before he could leave.

sentences.zh: 賜卹，贈內閣學士。

translations.literal: Mourning favors were granted, and he was posthumously made a grand secretary of the Inner Court.
translations.idiomatic: Mourning honors were granted, and he was posthumously made a grand secretary of the Inner Court.

sentences.zh: 陳湜，字舫仙，湖南湘鄉人。

translations.literal: Chen Shi, courtesy name Fangxian, was a native of Xiangxiang in Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Shi, styled Fangxian, came from Xiangxiang in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 咸豐六年，曾國荃赴援江西，招湜襄軍事，從克安福、萬安。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Xianfeng Zeng Guoquan went to aid Jiangxi, recruited Shi to assist in military affairs, and followed in the capture of Anfu and Wan'an.
translations.idiomatic: In 1856 Zeng Guoquan marched to aid Jiangxi, brought Shi into his staff, and took Anfu and Wan'an.

sentences.zh: 七年，進圍吉安。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he advanced to besiege Ji'an.
translations.idiomatic: In 1857 he pressed the siege of Ji'an.

sentences.zh: 國荃奔喪去軍，湜代領其眾。

translations.literal: Guoquan left the army to observe mourning for his father; Shi took command of his forces in his place.
translations.idiomatic: When Guoquan went home for his father's mourning, Shi took command of his troops.

sentences.zh: 尋以父憂歸。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he returned home on account of mourning for his father.
translations.idiomatic: He soon went home to mourn his father.

sentences.zh: 八年，從蔣益澧援廣西，克平樂。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he followed Jiang Yili to aid Guangxi and captured Pingle.
translations.idiomatic: In 1858 he followed Jiang Yili to Guangxi and took Pingle.

sentences.zh: 賊趨桂林，湜率四營遏之於大灣車埠，敗之，乘勝劃蘇橋壘。

translations.literal: Rebels marched on Guilin; Shi led four battalions to block them at Dawanchebu, defeated them, and taking advantage of victory leveled the stockade at Suqiao.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels moved on Guilin, Shi led four battalions to stop them at Dawanchebu, routed them, and pressed on to destroy the fort at Suqiao.

sentences.zh: 從攻柳州，克潯州。

translations.literal: He followed in the attack on Liuzhou and captured Xunzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He joined the assault on Liuzhou and took Xunzhou.

sentences.zh: 九年，石達開圍寶慶，湜募千人出祁陽赴援，與李續宜夾擊破之。

translations.literal: In the ninth year Shi Dakai besieged Baoqing; Shi recruited a thousand men, marched out from Qiyang to aid, and together with Li Xuyi defeated them in a pincer.
translations.idiomatic: In 1859, when Shi Dakai besieged Baoqing, Shi raised a thousand men from Qiyang, joined Li Xuyi in a converging attack, and broke the siege.

sentences.zh: 十年，曾國荃圍安慶，使湜總軍事。

translations.literal: In the tenth year Zeng Guoquan besieged Anqing and made Shi overall commander of military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In 1860, when Zeng Guoquan besieged Anqing, he put Shi in charge of the campaign.

sentences.zh: 湜規地形，請堨樅陽口蓄水阻援賊，力扼集賢關，從之。

translations.literal: Shi surveyed the terrain and requested damming Zongyang Mouth to store water and block relief rebels, and to hold Jixian Pass with all his strength; this was adopted.
translations.idiomatic: Shi studied the ground and proposed damming Zongyang Mouth to flood the approaches and block relief columns while holding Jixian Pass hard; his plan was adopted.

sentences.zh: 賊酋陳玉成來援，阻水，趨集賢關，擊破之。

translations.literal: Rebel chieftain Chen Yucheng came to relieve; blocked by water, he hastened toward Jixian Pass and was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: When rebel chief Chen Yucheng came to relieve the city, the flooded ground blocked him; he turned toward Jixian Pass and was beaten off.

sentences.zh: 十一年，克安慶，自是獨領一軍。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year Anqing was taken, and from then on he commanded an army alone.
translations.idiomatic: In 1861 Anqing fell, and from then on he commanded his own army.

sentences.zh: 循江而東，會克諸城隘，累​​擢至道員。

translations.literal: He followed the river eastward, joined in capturing various cities and passes, and through repeated promotions rose to circuit commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He marched downriver, helped take town after town along the way, and rose by stages to circuit commissioner.

sentences.zh: 同治元年，從國荃攻江寧，建議先並力九洑洲，斷江北接濟，先後會諸軍擊走李秀成、李世賢援眾。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tongzhi he followed Guoquan in attacking Jiangning, advised first concentrating strength on Jiufu Isle to cut north-of-the-river supplies, and in succession joined the armies in driving off the relief forces of Li Xiucheng and Li Shixian.
translations.idiomatic: In 1862 he followed Guoquan in the assault on Nanjing, urged that they first concentrate on Jiufu Isle to sever supplies from north of the river, and helped drive off the relief columns of Li Xiucheng and Li Shixian.

sentences.zh: 二年，城圍合，湜當西路，克江東橋、七甕橋、紫金山諸隘，賜號著勇巴圖魯。

translations.literal: In the second year the siege was closed; Shi held the western sector, captured Jiangdong Bridge, Qiweng Bridge, Purple Mountain, and other passes, and was granted the title Zhuoyong Batulu.
translations.idiomatic: In 1863 the ring closed; Shi held the west, took Jiangdong Bridge, Qiweng Bridge, Purple Mountain, and other passes, and was awarded the Manchu title Zhuoyong Batulu.

sentences.zh: 三年六月，克江寧，湜入旱西門，遇李秀成率死黨出走，逆擊反奔，尋為他軍所擒，以按察使記名。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the third year Jiangning was taken; Shi entered Hanxi Gate, met Li Xiucheng leading diehards in flight, turned to strike and drove them back, and soon he was captured by another army; Shi was entered on the list for provincial surveillance commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of 1864 Nanjing fell; Shi entered Hanxi Gate, met Li Xiucheng fleeing with his hard core, turned and drove them back, and Li was soon taken by another column; Shi was placed on the list for provincial surveillance commissioner.

sentences.zh: 四年，授陝西按察使，調山西。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was appointed Shaanxi provincial surveillance commissioner and transferred to Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: In 1865 he was appointed provincial surveillance commissioner of Shaanxi and transferred to Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 捻匪方熾，陳籌防五策，建水師於龍門、砥柱間。

translations.literal: Nian rebels were then raging; he memorialized five plans for defense and proposed establishing a navy between Longmen and Dizhu.
translations.idiomatic: With the Nian rebels at their height, he submitted five defensive plans and proposed a river flotilla between Longmen and Dizhu.

sentences.zh: 五年，捻酋張總愚謀渡渭，湜令水師焚三河口浮橋，督民團備渭北，賊不得逞。

translations.literal: In the fifth year Nian chieftain Zhang Zongyu planned to cross the Wei; Shi ordered the navy to burn the pontoon bridge at Sanhekou, supervised local militia to guard north of the Wei, and the rebels could not carry out their plan.
translations.idiomatic: In 1866 the Nian chief Zhang Zongyu tried to cross the Wei; Shi had the fleet burn the pontoon at Sanhekou, organized militia north of the Wei, and blocked the crossing.

sentences.zh: 六年，命湜駐汾州，節制文武。

translations.literal: In the sixth year Shi was ordered to garrison Fenzhou and control civil and military officials.
translations.idiomatic: In 1867 he was ordered to garrison Fenzhou with authority over civil and military officials.

sentences.zh: 冬，總愚乘河冰合，竄入山西，七年春，犯畿輔。

translations.literal: In winter Zongyu took advantage of the frozen river to flee into Shanxi; in the spring of the seventh year he invaded the capital region.
translations.idiomatic: That winter Zongyu crossed the frozen river into Shanxi; in the spring of 1868 he struck the capital region.

sentences.zh: 湜以疏防褫職，譴戍新疆，巡撫鄭敦謹疏請留防。

translations.literal: Shi was stripped of office for negligent defense and condemned to service in Xinjiang; Governor Zheng Dunjin memorialized to keep him on defense.
translations.idiomatic: He was dismissed for negligent defense and ordered to Xinjiang; Governor Zheng Dunjin asked that he be kept on defensive duty.

sentences.zh: 冬，陝回將乘隙渡河，屢擊走之，詔免發遣。

translations.literal: In winter Shaanxi Muslim forces tried to cross the river; he repeatedly drove them off, and an edict exempted him from banishment.
translations.idiomatic: That winter Shaanxi Muslim forces tried to cross the river; he beat them back repeatedly, and an edict spared him exile.

sentences.zh: 左宗棠西征，檄湜率五營出固原，斷漢伯堡賊南趨河州之道，殲餘彥祿餘黨於羅家嶮。

translations.literal: Zuo Zongtang's western campaign ordered Shi to lead five battalions out of Guyuan to cut the route by which rebels at Hanbobao might march south toward Hezhou, and destroyed the remnant band of Yu Yanlu at Luojiaxian.
translations.idiomatic: On Zuo Zongtang's western campaign, Shi led five battalions from Guyuan to block the road south from Hanbobao toward Hezhou and wiped out Yu Yanlu's remnant band at Luojiaxian.

sentences.zh: 九年，金積堡平，復原官。

translations.literal: In the ninth year Jinjibao was pacified and his original office was restored.
translations.idiomatic: In 1870 Jinjibao fell and his former rank was restored.

sentences.zh: 十年，進規河州，宗棠令湜盡護諸將渡洮進攻。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, advancing on Hezhou, Zongtang ordered Shi to escort all generals across the Tao for the assault.
translations.idiomatic: In 1871, in the advance on Hezhou, Zongtang had Shi escort the generals across the Tao for the attack.

sentences.zh: 連克陳家山、楊家山、董家山諸回堡，逼攻太子寺老巢，破其外壕。

translations.literal: In succession he captured the Muslim forts at Chenjiashan, Yangjiashan, and Dongjiashan, pressed the attack on the old nest at Taizisi, and broke its outer moat.
translations.idiomatic: He took the Muslim forts at Chenjiashan, Yangjiashan, and Dongjiashan in turn, pressed Taizisi, and breached its outer defenses.

sentences.zh: 十一年，提督傅先宗等戰歿，賊乘勝來攻。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year Provincial Commander Fu Xianzong and others died in battle, and rebels took advantage of victory to attack.
translations.idiomatic: In 1872 Provincial Commander Fu Xianzong and others were killed, and the enemy pressed the attack.

sentences.zh: 湜陽置酒高會，密令總兵沈玉遂急搗之，馬占鼇窮蹙乞降，縛悍酋狗齒牙子等以獻。

translations.literal: Shi openly set out wine for a great gathering, secretly ordered Brigadier Shen Yusui to strike urgently; Ma Zhan'ao, pressed hard, begged to surrender and bound the fierce chieftain Gou Chiya and others to present.
translations.idiomatic: Shi gave a lavish banquet while secretly ordering Brigadier Shen Yusui to strike; Ma Zhan'ao, cornered, surrendered and sent the fierce chief Gou Chiya and others bound as captives.

sentences.zh: 河州平。

translations.literal: Hezhou was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Hezhou was pacified.

sentences.zh: 十二年，叛酋馬桂源、馬本源踞巴燕戎格，湜率軍進討，二酋敗遁。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year rebel chiefs Ma Guiyuan and Ma Benyuan held Bayan Rongge; Shi led the army forward to suppress them and the two chiefs were defeated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: In 1873 rebel chiefs Ma Guiyuan and Ma Benyuan held Bayan Rongge; Shi advanced against them and they were beaten and fled.

sentences.zh: 湜善視其孥，遂因佔鼇來降，數其罪誅之，並斬馬五麻諸悍目，賜號奇車伯巴圖魯。

translations.literal: Shi treated their families kindly; then because Zhan'ao came to surrender, he enumerated their crimes and executed them, and also beheaded the fierce leaders Ma Wuma and others; he was granted the title Qichebo Batulu.
translations.idiomatic: He treated their families well; when Zhan'ao surrendered he listed their crimes and executed them, beheaded fierce leaders including Ma Wuma, and was awarded the Manchu title Qichebo Batulu.

sentences.zh: 四月，逾河收循化。

translations.literal: In the fourth month he crossed the river and recovered Xunhua.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month he crossed the river and recovered Xunhua.

sentences.zh: 循化撒拉回素獷悍，恃險擾邊。

translations.literal: The Salar Muslims of Xunhua had long been fierce and bold, relying on difficult terrain to harass the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: The Salar Muslims of Xunhua were notoriously fierce and used the terrain to raid the frontier.

sentences.zh: 湜深入其阻，群回縛悍目馬十八、沈五十七等二十餘人獻軍前，繳械受約束。

translations.literal: Shi penetrated their strongholds; the Muslim communities bound the fierce leaders Ma Shiba, Shen Wushiqi, and more than twenty others and presented them before the army, surrendering weapons and accepting restraint.
translations.idiomatic: He penetrated their strongholds; the communities bound fierce leaders Ma Shiba, Shen Wushiqi, and more than twenty others and brought them in, surrendering arms and accepting terms.

sentences.zh: 湜規地勢，修城設官，分營扼駐，與西寧、碾伯、河州聲息相通焉。

translations.literal: Shi surveyed the terrain, repaired walls and established officials, divided camps to hold key points, and communications were linked with Xining, Nianbo, and Hezhou.
translations.idiomatic: He surveyed the ground, rebuilt walls, posted officials, garrisoned key points, and linked communications with Xining, Nianbo, and Hezhou.

sentences.zh: 尋謝軍事回籍。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he resigned military duties and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: He soon left the army and returned home.

sentences.zh: 光緒八年，兩江總督曾國荃奏調統水陸諸軍，兼治海防，駐軍吳淞。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Guangxu Governor-General Zeng Guoquan of the Two Jiangs memorialized to transfer him to command land and naval forces and also manage coastal defense, encamping at Wusong.
