translations.idiomatic: In 1882 Governor-General Zeng Guoquan requested his transfer to command land and naval forces and coastal defense, with headquarters at Wusong.

sentences.zh: 以私行遊宴被劾歸。

translations.literal: He was impeached and sent home for private excursions and banqueting.
translations.idiomatic: He was impeached and sent home for unauthorized pleasure outings.

sentences.zh: 十二年，復出統南洋兵輪，總湘、淮諸軍營務，授江蘇按察使。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he again came out to command the southern ocean steam fleet, oversee Hunan and Huai army affairs, and was appointed Jiangsu provincial surveillance commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In 1886 he again took command of the southern steam fleet and Hunan-Huai army affairs and was appointed provincial surveillance commissioner of Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 二十年，遼東兵事起，詔集舊部防山海關，移屯關外鞍山站。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year, when war broke out in Liaodong, an edict gathered his old troops to defend Shanhaiguan and shifted camp to Anshan Station outside the pass.
translations.idiomatic: In 1894, when war broke out in Liaodong, he was ordered to gather his old troops at Shanhaiguan and moved to Anshan Station beyond the pass.

sentences.zh: 二十一年春，進駐大高嶺，遣將援遼陽。

translations.literal: In the spring of the twenty-first year he advanced to Dagao Ridge and sent generals to aid Liaoyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of 1895 he advanced to Dagao Ridge and sent generals to relieve Liaoyang.

sentences.zh: 和議成，擢江西布政使。

translations.literal: When peace was made he was promoted to Jiangxi provincial administration commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: After peace was concluded he was promoted to provincial administration commissioner of Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 命剿甘肅叛回，未行，复駐山海關。

translations.literal: He was ordered to suppress Gansu rebel Muslims but before departing was again stationed at Shanhaiguan.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to suppress rebel Muslims in Gansu but was again posted to Shanhaiguan before he could leave.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，卒，贈太子少保。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year he died and was posthumously made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In 1896 he died and was posthumously made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 湜從曾國荃最久，後屢蹶，仕久不進。

translations.literal: Shi had followed Zeng Guoquan longest; afterward he stumbled repeatedly and long service brought little advancement.
translations.idiomatic: Shi had served Zeng Guoquan longer than anyone, but later suffered repeated setbacks and advanced slowly despite long service.

sentences.zh: 世稱為宿將，光緒中，命繪中興功臣於紫光閣，徵集諸將之像，湜與焉。

translations.literal: The age called him a veteran general; in the Guangxu period, when portraits of meritorious ministers of the restoration were painted in the Hall of Purple Splendor, Shi's likeness was among them.
translations.idiomatic: He was known as a veteran commander; in the Guangxu era, when portraits of restoration heroes were painted in the Hall of Purple Splendor, his was included.

sentences.zh: 李元度，字次青，湖南平江人。

translations.literal: Li Yuandu, courtesy name Ciqing, was a native of Pingjiang in Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yuandu, styled Ciqing, came from Pingjiang in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 以舉人官黔陽教諭。

translations.literal: As a provincial graduate he served as instructor of Qianyang.
translations.idiomatic: As a provincial graduate he served as instructor of Qianyang.

sentences.zh: 曾國籓在籍治團練，元度上書數千言言兵事，國籓壯之，招入幕。

translations.literal: When Zeng Guofan organized local militia in his native place, Yuandu submitted a memorial of several thousand characters on military affairs; Guofan was impressed and recruited him into his staff.
translations.idiomatic: When Zeng Guofan organized militia at home, Yuandu sent a long memorial on military affairs; Guofan was impressed and took him onto his staff.

sentences.zh: 咸豐五年，國籓移軍江西，令元度募勇三千屯湖口。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Xianfeng Guofan moved his army to Jiangxi and ordered Yuandu to raise three thousand braves and encamp at Hukou.
translations.idiomatic: In 1855 Guofan moved into Jiangxi and had Yuandu raise three thousand men and encamp at Hukou.

sentences.zh: 六年，移屯撫州，偕江軍林源恩合防。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he shifted camp to Fuzhou and together with Jiang army commander Lin Yuan'en combined in defense.
translations.idiomatic: In 1856 he moved to Fuzhou and joined Jiang forces under Lin Yuan'en in the defense.

sentences.zh: 與賊相持久之，餉絀，分軍克宜黃、崇仁；

translations.literal: He faced the rebels in a long stalemate; pay was short, and he divided his army to capture Yihuang and Chongren.
translations.idiomatic: He held the rebels in a long stalemate; funds ran short, and he detached columns to take Yihuang and Chongren.

sentences.zh: 而賊自景德來援，撫州賊出攻江軍營，林源恩死之。

translations.literal: But rebels came from Jingde to relieve them, and Fuzhou rebels sallied to attack the Jiang army camp; Lin Yuan'en died.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels from Jingde came to their aid, and Fuzhou rebels struck the Jiang camp; Lin Yuan'en was killed.

sentences.zh: 元度突圍出，移屯貴溪，防廣信。

translations.literal: Yuandu broke out of the encirclement, shifted camp to Guixi, and defended Guangxin.
translations.idiomatic: Yuandu broke out, moved to Guixi, and held Guangxin.

sentences.zh: 七年，賊二萬來襲玉山，守卒僅七百人，元度迎戰，斷賊浮梁，賊以步隊綴軍，騎賊趨上游跐水渡。

translations.literal: In the seventh year twenty thousand rebels came to assault Yushan; the garrison was only seven hundred men; Yuandu met them in battle, cut the rebels' pontoon at Fuliang, the rebels used infantry to delay the army while cavalry hurried upstream to wade across.
translations.idiomatic: In 1857 twenty thousand rebels attacked Yushan; only seven hundred men held the town; Yuandu fought them, cut their pontoon at Fuliang, while infantry delayed his force and cavalry forded upstream.

sentences.zh: 乃回城拒守，被攻兩晝夜，元度立埤兒間，彈中左頰。

translations.literal: He then returned to the city to defend; after two days and nights of assault Yuandu stood among the parapets and a bullet struck his left cheek.
translations.idiomatic: He fell back to defend the city; after two days and nights of assault he stood on the wall and a bullet struck his left cheek.

sentences.zh: 賊忽罷攻，鉦鐃雜作，知其穴地道，乃掘壕以防，伺其穿隧及壕殪之。

translations.literal: The rebels suddenly ceased the attack and gongs and cymbals sounded together; knowing they were mining, he dug a trench for defense, waited until their tunnel reached the trench, and killed them.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels suddenly stopped and sounded gongs and cymbals; knowing they were mining, he dug a trench, and when their tunnel reached it he killed the miners.

sentences.zh: 賊技窮引去，伏兵邀擊，安仁、弋陽、廣信皆平。

translations.literal: The rebels' stratagems exhausted, they withdrew; ambush troops intercepted them, and Anren, Yiyang, and Guangxin were all pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Their tricks exhausted, they withdrew; ambush troops cut them off, and Anren, Yiyang, and Guangxin were pacified.

sentences.zh: 元度先已累擢知府，以道員記名，至是加按察使銜，賜號色爾固楞巴圖魯。

translations.literal: Yuandu had already been promoted repeatedly to prefect and entered on the list as circuit commissioner; now he was given the brevet rank of provincial surveillance commissioner and granted the title Se'erguleng Batulu.
translations.idiomatic: He had already risen to prefect and been entered for circuit commissioner; now he received the brevet rank of provincial surveillance commissioner and the Manchu title Se'erguleng Batulu.

sentences.zh: 八年，率所部平江軍援浙江，敗賊玉山子午口。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he led his Pingjiang army to aid Zhejiang and defeated rebels at Ziwukou in Yushan.
translations.idiomatic: In 1858 he led his Pingjiang troops to Zhejiang and defeated the enemy at Ziwukou in Yushan.

sentences.zh: 會克常山、江山，授浙江溫處道。

translations.literal: He joined in capturing Changshan and Jiangshan and was appointed intendant of the Wenzhou-Chuzhou circuit in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: He helped take Changshan and Jiangshan and was appointed intendant of the Wenzhou-Chuzhou circuit.

sentences.zh: 十年，曾國籓督師皖南，調元度安徽寧池太道，防徽州。

translations.literal: In the tenth year Zeng Guofan directed the army in southern Anhui and transferred Yuandu to the Ningchi-Taizhou circuit in Anhui to defend Huizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In 1860 Zeng Guofan directed operations in southern Anhui and transferred Yuandu to the Ningchi-Taizhou intendant post to defend Huizhou.

sentences.zh: 至甫三日，賊由旌德糾合土匪散軍入績溪叢山關。

translations.literal: He had been there only three days when rebels from Jingde joined local bandits and scattered troops to enter Congshan Pass in Jixi.
translations.idiomatic: He had been there only three days when rebels from Jingde, with local bandits and scattered troops, entered Congshan Pass in Jixi.

sentences.zh: 遣同知童梅華、都司單綏福率千人往援，敗挫。

translations.literal: He sent Subprefect Tong Meihua and Commander Shan Suifu with a thousand men to aid them; they were defeated.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Subprefect Tong Meihua and Commander Shan Suifu with a thousand men; they were beaten.

sentences.zh: 賊趨郡城，元度退走。

translations.literal: Rebels marched on the prefectural city and Yuandu retreated.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels marched on the prefectural seat and Yuandu fell back.

sentences.zh: 國籓奏劾，褫職逮治。

translations.literal: Guofan memorialized to impeach him, stripped him of office, and ordered arrest and trial.
translations.idiomatic: Guofan impeached him, stripped his rank, and ordered his arrest.

sentences.zh: 會浙江巡撫王有齡奏調援浙，元度不待命，回籍募勇八千，號安越軍。

translations.literal: When Zhejiang Governor Wang Youqin memorialized to transfer him to aid Zhejiang, Yuandu did not await orders, returned home to raise eight thousand braves, called the Anyue Army.
translations.idiomatic: When Governor Wang Youqin of Zhejiang requested him for the relief of Zhejiang, Yuandu did not wait for orders, went home, raised eight thousand men as the Anyue Army.

sentences.zh: 將行，粵匪犯湖南，巡撫文格留其軍守瀏陽，偕諸軍破賊，詔賞還按察使銜，並加布政使銜。

translations.literal: As he was about to depart, Guangdong rebels invaded Hunan; Governor Wenge kept his army to defend Liuyang; together with other armies he defeated the rebels; an edict restored his brevet provincial surveillance commissioner rank and also added brevet provincial administration commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: As he was about to march, Guangdong rebels entered Hunan; Governor Wenge kept his troops at Liuyang; with other forces he defeated the rebels; an edict restored his brevet provincial surveillance commissioner rank and added brevet provincial administration commissioner.

sentences.zh: 會杭州陷，王有齡死，詔左宗棠代之。

translations.literal: When Hangzhou fell and Wang Youqin died, an edict replaced him with Zuo Zongtang.
translations.idiomatic: When Hangzhou fell and Wang Youqin died, Zuo Zongtang was appointed in his place.

sentences.zh: 元度率軍入浙，與李定太守衢州，授浙江鹽運使，署布政使。

translations.literal: Yuandu led his army into Zhejiang, joined Li Ding in defending Quzhou, was appointed Zhejiang salt transport commissioner, and acted as provincial administration commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Yuandu marched into Zhejiang, joined Li Ding in holding Quzhou, was made salt transport commissioner of Zhejiang, and served as acting provincial administration commissioner.

sentences.zh: 國籓以元度罪未定，不聽勘遽回籍，复劾革職，交左宗棠差遣。

translations.literal: Guofan, because Yuandu's guilt was not yet settled, would not allow him to leave his post and hurry home, again impeached him and stripped office, and handed him over to Zuo Zongtang for assignment.
translations.idiomatic: Guofan, holding that Yuandu's case was unsettled, objected to his leaving for home, impeached him again, stripped his rank, and placed him under Zuo Zongtang's orders.

sentences.zh: 言官再論劾，命國籓、宗棠按治。

translations.literal: Censorial officials attacked him again; he was ordered to be investigated by Guofan and Zongtang.
translations.idiomatic: Censors attacked him again; Guofan and Zongtang were ordered to investigate.

sentences.zh: 國籓奏：「徽州之失，元度甫至，情有可原。

translations.literal: Guofan memorialized: "In the loss of Huizhou, Yuandu had only just arrived; there is reason to excuse him."
translations.idiomatic: Guofan wrote: "In the loss of Huizhou, Yuandu had only just arrived; that may be excused."

sentences.zh: 」宗棠疏言：「杭州失陷，非因其逗留所致。

translations.literal: Zongtang memorialized: "The fall of Hangzhou was not caused by his delay."
translations.idiomatic: Zongtang wrote: "Hangzhou did not fall because he lingered."

sentences.zh: 惟落職後求去索餉，不顧大局。

translations.literal: But after losing office he sought to leave and demanded pay without regard for the larger situation.
translations.idiomatic: But after losing office he demanded pay and tried to leave without regard to the larger situation.

sentences.zh: 」論遣戍。

translations.literal: He was sentenced to banishment.
translations.idiomatic: He was sentenced to exile.

sentences.zh: 沈葆楨、李鴻章、彭玉麟、鮑超等交章薦其才，代繳台費，免罪歸。

translations.literal: Shen Baozhen, Li Hongzhang, Peng Yulin, Bao Chao, and others jointly recommended his talent and paid his Taiwan fee on his behalf; he was pardoned and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Baozhen, Li Hongzhang, Peng Yulin, Bao Chao, and others recommended him and paid his Taiwan fee; he was pardoned and returned.

sentences.zh: 同治初，貴州巡撫張亮基奏起剿教匪，以功復原官，擢雲南按察使。

translations.literal: Early in Tongzhi, Guizhou Governor Zhang Liangji memorialized to recall him to suppress sectarian rebels; through merit his original office was restored and he was promoted to Yunnan provincial surveillance commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Tongzhi, Guizhou Governor Zhang Liangji recalled him to fight sect rebels; by merit his rank was restored and he was promoted to provincial surveillance commissioner of Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 光緒八年，丁母憂。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Guangxu he observed mourning for his mother.
translations.idiomatic: In 1882 he went into mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 服闋，補貴州按察使，遷布政使。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he was appointed Guizhou provincial surveillance commissioner and transferred to provincial administration commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning he was appointed provincial surveillance commissioner of Guizhou and then provincial administration commissioner.

sentences.zh: 十三年，卒於官。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: In 1887 he died in office.

sentences.zh: 元度擅文章，好言兵，然自將屢僨事。

translations.literal: Yuandu excelled at literary composition and liked to discuss military affairs, yet when he commanded troops himself he often failed.
translations.idiomatic: Yuandu was a gifted writer and fond of military theory, yet as a field commander he often failed.

sentences.zh: 所著先正事略、天嶽山館文集，並行世。

translations.literal: His works Xianzheng Shilue and Tianyue Shan'guan Wenji both circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: His works Records of Former Worthies and Collected Writings from the Tianyue Mountain Studio both circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 論曰：蕭啟江、張運蘭功在江西，在湘軍中資勞最深，中道而殞，故卹典特隆。

translations.literal: The appraisal says: The merit of Xiao Qijiang and Zhang Yunlan lay in Jiangxi; among the Hunan army their seniority in service was deepest; they died mid-course, and therefore mourning favors were especially generous.
translations.idiomatic: The appraisal says: Xiao Qijiang and Zhang Yunlan won their fame in Jiangxi; among Hunan troops their seniority was greatest; they died young, and so mourning honors were especially generous.

sentences.zh: 唐訓方、蔣凝學轉戰功多，舊部散亡，再出遂不競。

translations.literal: Tang Xunfang and Jiang Ningxue won many victories in successive campaigns, but when their old troops dispersed and they came out again they could not compete.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Xunfang and Jiang Ningxue fought many successful campaigns, but once their old troops were gone they could not match their earlier record.

sentences.zh: 陳湜、李元度皆躓而復起。

translations.literal: Chen Shi and Li Yuandu both stumbled and rose again.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Shi and Li Yuandu both fell and rose again.

sentences.zh: 元度文學之士，所行不逮其言，軍中猶以宿望推之爾。

translations.literal: Yuandu was a man of letters; his conduct did not match his words, yet in the army he was still esteemed for long standing.
translations.idiomatic: Yuandu was a literary man whose deeds fell short of his words, yet the army still respected his long service.
